title: Fidelity correlation benchmarking playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
------
This playbook describes a repeatable process to benchmark correlation between model fidelity (quality) and runtime execution signals (latency, kernel selection, memory pressure, quantization path) across production-like workloads. The goal is to produce actionable correlations that guide scheduler, kernel, and quantization changes without regressing customer-visible quality.

Why this doc exists
-------------------
- Engineers often optimize for cost/latency and see unexpected changes in output quality.
- Quantitative correlation between fidelity metrics and runtime signals helps make safe tradeoffs.
- This playbook standardizes experiment design, telemetry collection, and analysis so that findings can be validated and operationalized.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Audience: runtime engineers, benchmarking owners, SREs, model-onboarding team.
- Scope: inference workloads for text generation and chat; includes model variants, quantized kernels, and multi-tenant scheduling shapes.
- Out of scope: training fidelity analysis, dataset labeling methodology outside of our eval harness.

Key definitions
---------------
- Fidelity: end-to-end task quality measured by an agreed prompt set and evaluation metric (e.g., BLEU, ROUGE, or Redwood QA score).
- Runtime signal: telemetry emitted by the runtime (per-request latency percentiles, kernel variant id, slot preemption count, KV cache hit rate, accelerator occupancy).
- Correlation window: time window used to align telemetry and fidelity observations (default: 1 hour for production mirroring tests, 5–15 minutes for synthetic load tests).

Required tooling and infra
------------------------
- Benchmark runner: benchmarking-and-perf-suite/runner v2.1 (supports traffic shaping and mixed concurrency).
- Eval harness: eval-harness/cli v0.9 for automated fidelity scoring against standardized prompt sets.
- Trace collector: tracing pipeline (OTLP -> internal collector) with the kernel and scheduler annotations enabled.
- Shadow traffic mirror: network mirror that can replay production traffic into an isolated runtime fleet.
- Metrics store: Prometheus + long-term rollup in ClickHouse for hourly aggregates.

Pre-experiment checklist
------------------------
1. Confirm owner: assign an experiment owner and at least one reviewer (SRE + model owner).
2. Select prompt set: choose a representative prompt set from prompt-sets-and-benchmarks labeled with the workload fingerprint.
3. Baseline health: ensure SLAs on baseline fleet (p90 < target latency, error rate < 0.1%).
4. Telemetry sanity: verify trace and metric tags are present: model_version, kernel_variant, scheduling_slot_id, shard_id, quantization_profile.
5. Dependencies: confirm benchmark runner and eval harness versions in the experiment README.

Experiment matrix design
------------------------
Design a factorial matrix to isolate effects. Common factors:
- Model variant: full-precision, 8-bit quantized, mixed-precision.
- Kernel variant: tensor-core fast-path, fallback kernel, sparse-attention kernel.
- Scheduling policy: fairness-first, latency-priority, batch-aggressive.
- Load shape: steady-state low-concurrency, bursty peak, long-sequence heavy.

Matrix example (4x3x3x3 = 108 runs):
| Factor | Values |
|--|--|
| Model variant | fp16, int8, int8+kv
| Kernel variant | fast, fallback, sparse
| Scheduling policy | fairness, latency, burst
| Load shape | steady, burst, long

Data collection and alignment
-----------------------------
1. Start metric capture and trace collection for all candidate fleets.
2. Run the benchmark runner to generate controlled traffic for each matrix cell. Ensure a warmup period of at least 10 minutes to stabilize KV caches and batch patterns.
3. Simultaneously run the eval harness against the same prompt set and collect fidelity scores. For stochastic models run N=5 seeds and aggregate mean/CI.
4. Aggregate telemetry into hourly buckets and align with fidelity scores using the correlation window. Use request IDs or hash(provenance) for per-request joining when available.

Primary metrics to collect (per request)
- latency_ms (p50, p90, p99)
- kernel_variant_id
- kernel_execution_time_ms
- kv_cache_hit (boolean)
- batch_size
- accelerator_util_pct
- quantization_profile
- model_version
- fidelity_score (from eval harness)

Analysis procedure
------------------
1. Exploratory data checks: confirm distributions, missing telemetry, and outliers.
2. Correlation analysis: compute Spearman and Pearson correlations between fidelity_score and each runtime signal. Report 95% confidence intervals.
3. Conditional effects: use stratified analysis (e.g., p99 latency when kv_cache_hit=false) to identify interaction effects.
4. Simple causal checks: run ablated tests (flip single factor while holding others constant) and validate delta fidelity.
5. Regression detection: if any metric change co-occurs with fidelity drop > threshold (see threshold table) escalate to a quality hold.

Thresholds and decision rules
----------------------------
| Signal | Alert threshold | Action |
|--|--|--|
| p99 latency | +20% vs baseline | Investigate scheduler backlog and kernel slow-paths
| fidelity_score | -2.0 points absolute (task-specific) | Block rollout, start joint triage (runtime + model owner)
| kv_cache_hit_rate | -10 percentage points | Check cache affinity and warmstart profiles
| kernel_fallback_rate | > 5% | Evaluate kernel correctness and performance regressions

Recommended default fidelity thresholds (examples):
- Short-form summarization: delta ROUGE-L <= 1.5 absolute
- Q&A fidelity (Redwood QA): delta <= 2 points

Reporting and artifacts
-----------------------
Every experiment must produce a single artifact bundle:
- experiment-manifest.yml (matrix, versions, runner config)
- telemetry-rollup.csv (hourly aggregates)
- fidelity-results.json (per-prompt scores and seed stats)
- analysis-notebook.ipynb (minimum reproducible notebook with the correlation figures)
- triage-log.md (if any thresholds are breached)
Upload artifacts to the experiment bucket: s3://redwood-experiments/fidelity-correlation/{yyyyMMdd}_{owner}_{id}.

Operationalization path
-----------------------
1. If correlations show a safe optimization (e.g., int8 reduces cost with < threshold fidelity delta), prepare a controlled rollout plan.
2. Create a runtime feature flag for the kernel/quantization change.
3. Run a canary with mirrored traffic for 48 hours and validate metrics.
4. Use the Redwood Console route-level QA gating: require fidelity_score check to pass on canary before expanding.

Escalation and triage playbook
------------------------------
1. If fidelity threshold is breached, pause rollout and notify: #runtime-incidents, model-owner, and release manager.
2. Triage steps:
   a. Confirm telemetry alignment and timestamps.
   b. Run targeted replay for failing prompt subset (use experiment-manifest filters).
   c. Check kernel logs for errors or fallback signatures.
   d. Assess whether degradation is deterministic or stochastic across seeds.
3. Rollback criteria: complete rollback if fidelity delta persists after 3 targeted replay attempts or if customers report reproducible failures.

Troubleshooting FAQ
-------------------
- Q: My fidelity score is noisy across runs. A: Increase sample seeds to N>=10 and use median-of-means for robust estimates.
- Q: Kernel variant tags missing in traces. A: Ensure runtime build includes "kernel-annotator" and that trace sampling for the experiment is set to 100%.
- Q: Correlation but no causal signal. A: Run single-factor ablation (hold other variables constant) and verify reproducibility.

Appendix A — sample experiment-manifest.yml
------------------------------------------
experiment_id: fidelity-20260115-aisha
owner: aisha.patel@redwood.ai
matrix:
  model_variant: [fp16, int8]
  kernel_variant: [fast, fallback]
  scheduling: [latency, fairness]
  load_shape: [steady, burst]
runner_config:
  duration_minutes: 120
  warmup_minutes: 15
  concurrency_profile: steady-200
eval_config:
  prompt_set: summarization/clinical-abstracts-v2
  seeds: 5
  metric: rouge_l

Appendix B — example CLI commands
---------------------------------
# start telemetry capture
$ benchctl start-capture --experiment fidelity-20260115-aisha --tags "fidelity,playbook"

# run a single cell
$ benchctl run-cell --manifest experiment-manifest.yml --cell "model_variant=fp16,kernel_variant=fast, scheduling=latency"

# collect eval results
$ eval-harness run --config eval_config.yml --out fidelity-results.json
